body:
Part of #2526 (GPU shader toolpath generation). Slice 5 of 5. Needs #2621 (the drop-cutter filter).

Maintainer order (2026-11-18): "GPU shader issues get priority". Thus this issue is `P4`.

## Why
The browser build (#31) accepts WebGPU or WebGL2 (`crates/ui/src/egui_app/shell_web.rs` line 86). WebGL2 has no compute shaders. A browser cannot block on a GPU future, so the readback of the native path (`crates/ui/src/trace/readback.rs`, native only) does not work there. Slices #2620 and #2621 use the CPU path in the browser until this slice is done.

## What
- The compute crate of #2620 gets the async twins (`*_async`, as `headless_gpu::device_async` does today) for device, dispatch and readback.
- On WebGPU, the generate job awaits the filter result. On WebGL2, the capability probe says "no compute" and the CPU path runs. The log names the reason one time.
- WebGPU limits (`max_storage_buffer_binding_size` default 128 MiB) set the tile size. A tile past the limit is split or uses the CPU path. It is never truncated.

## Pinning tests (CPU reference)
- The wasm32 build compiles (`web/build-app-wasm.sh`).
- A native test drives the async path through `pollster` and gives the same `.cl` bytes as the CPU path on the 3D finishing goldens.
- A unit test of the probe: a WebGL2-like downlevel set gives "no compute".

## Decision entry
Not needed if no new crate edge is added.

Effort: `effort:high` (several crates, async GPU path; the output stays the CPU f64 value).

Done means: the browser build uses the GPU filter on WebGPU and the CPU path on WebGL2, the wasm build compiles, and the async path gives byte-equal output.
